raw_response:
I farm only 3.5 mu, so I will keep things simple, reliable, and manageable with my family labor. I have done wheat-maize for many years, and with well irrigation I will stay with that system because it is familiar and reduces my risk. Since some family members work off-farm, I will not choose anything too labor-intensive or experimental. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough fertilizer to secure a stable stand through winter and support grain filling, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about yield on my small area, and I will fertilize a bit more heavily than wheat, especially nitrogen, because maize responds well when water is available. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical for my small plot and fits how I would prepare land between the two crops. My goal this year is steady output, not taking big risks, and making sure the land gives me dependable grain for the household and income.
